slot.brief: Give a small set of 5–6 observations (small integers, mean an integer) and ask for the variance or standard deviation directly by computation.

stem: The standard deviation of the observations $5, 5, 6, 8, 9, 9$ is

verdicts.working: Mean = 7; the sum of squared deviations is 18. Dividing by 6 gives variance 3, so the standard deviation is √3.

working:
$\bar{x}=7$, $\sum (x_i-\bar{x})^2=18$; $\sigma=\sqrt{\dfrac{18}{6}}=\sqrt{3}$.

Independent check: Mean = 7; the sum of squared deviations is 18. Dividing by 6 gives variance 3, so the standard deviation is √3.
solution:
The mean is $\bar{x}=7$, and the sum of squared deviations is $18$. Hence,
$$\sigma=\sqrt{\frac{18}{6}}=\sqrt{3}$$
